body:
This record sets out the established scientific foundation: what is known, what the governing principles are, and where settled science ends and open questions begin. It covers Fully Autonomous Transportation Networks — Coordinated vehicle systems operating with limited direct human driving.

Transport technology is in a deployment phase for autonomy on roads and an R&D phase for autonomy in the air. High-speed ground concepts fight economics more than physics; electric aviation fights battery energy density; cities-as-systems fight institutional inertia. The demonstrated wins — driver assistance, metro automation, eVTOL test flights — are real and compounding. The speculative layer (supersonic point-to-point, floating cities, vacuum-tube intercity) needs honest cost-per-passenger-kilometer math before anything else.

Feasibility tier: EXPERIMENTALLY-SUPPORTED. Key components or narrow versions have been demonstrated in laboratories, prototypes, or limited deployments, but the full technology as described does not yet exist. Records at this tier separate what experiments have shown from what is extrapolated.

The established science behind Fully Autonomous Transportation Networks rests on Transport is applied energy and control: drag, rolling resistance, and propulsion efficiency set energy use; network theory and control set throughput and safety. At the experimentally-supported feasibility tier, the honest statement is this: the governing principles are understood in the laboratory, with open questions about how they behave at full scale and in integrated systems.
